---
name: abap-runtime-analysis
description: Analyze ABAP runtime incidents, debugger state, and performance symptoms using application logs, source/reference inspection, safe data reads, and authorized debugger sessions; runtime call relationships must be derived from source inspection (FindReferences/GetContext) because no call-graph tool is exposed, and dump/trace evidence must come from SAP tooling outside this addon. Use for diagnosing failures before or after ABAP/RAP code changes.
---

# ABAP runtime analysis

**Workspace preflight.** Whenever this workflow edits or hands off serialized ABAP sources in a workspace, run `LintABAPProject` (`lint_abap_project`) before sending changes to SAP; if unavailable, report the skipped preflight and use caller-supplied `LintABAP` if available. Confirm the configured root is the intended project (`SAP_AI_DEV_TOOLKIT_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, or the MCP process working directory by default; `directory` is relative to that root), `targetRelease` matches the SAP target, `dependencies.missingFolders` and `syntaxRules.disabled` are empty, and `status` is `clean`. `issues`, `incomplete`, `no-abap-files`, or a mismatched root/release are not passes. This is static analysis only and does not validate SAP activation or runtime; caller-supplied `LintABAP` on the latest source for the exact object set remains mandatory immediately before activation. Skip when no serialized project source exists.

## Tool shortlist

Query the active MCP server's live `tools/list` once and use the exact live names and schemas. Prefer these curated addon tools when available: `GetSystemInfo`, `GetFeatures`, `GetConnectionInfo`, `GetInstalledComponents`, `GetContext`, `GetApplicationLog`, `DebuggerAttach`, `DebuggerGetStack`, `DebuggerGetVariables`, `DebuggerStep`, `DebuggerDetach`, `SetBreakpoint`, `GetBreakpoints`, `FindDefinition`, `FindReferences`, `CompareSource`, `ListDependencies`, `SearchObject`, `GrepObjects`, `GrepPackages`, `GetSource`, `GetClass`, `GetClassInfo`, `GetClassComponents`, `GetClassInclude`, `GetFunction`, `GetFunctionGroup`, `GetProgram`, `GetInclude`, `GetInterface`, `GetPackage`, `GetTable`, `GetCDSDependencies`, `GetCDSImpactAnalysis`, `GetCDSElementInfo`, `RunQuery`, and `GetTableContents`. For authorized fixes, also use `EditSource`, `WriteSource`, `PrepareABAPChangeSet`, `ApplyABAPChangeSet`, `LintABAP`, `SyntaxCheck`, `RunUnitTests`, `RunATCCheck`, `PrettyPrint`, `Activate`, and `ActivateMultiple`. Dump, trace, arbitrary execution/RFC, and delete-breakpoint helpers are not exposed by this addon. Tool names shown in PascalCase (such as `GetSource` or `LintABAP`) are logical names; the live MCP surface exposes them as lowercase snake_case. A server scoped to a single destination (the normal case for generated `mcp.json` entries) exposes them unprefixed, so `GetSource` appears as `get_source` and `LintABAP` as `lint_abap`; when several destinations share one server, each name is destination-prefixed with its slug for disambiguation (for example `cfd_run_query`). Always call the exact names returned by `tools/list`.

Use `GetStructure`, `GetTypeInfo`, and `GetMessages` for read-only DDIC, ABAP type, and message-class context during runtime analysis.

1. Establish incident boundaries: symptom, expected result, object/service, destination, user/session, input, time window, frequency, and whether reproduction/debugging is authorized.
2. Gather read-only evidence first. Correlate logs, source/reference context, dependencies, debugger state, and data conditions by timestamp and object path. Do not start with source edits.
3. For debugger sessions, set breakpoints sparingly — breakpoints registered with `SetBreakpoint` cannot be deleted through this surface because `DeleteBreakpoint` is not exposed — and attach only to the authorized session. Inspect stack and variables, step minimally, then detach; `DebuggerDetach` releases the session. Never attach to another user's unrelated session.
4. For performance symptoms, separate database access, ABAP logic, remote calls, locking, and payload/serialization cost using available source/data evidence and measured reproduction evidence. If dumps or traces are required, hand them off to SAP tooling outside this addon.
5. Convert evidence into a falsifiable root-cause chain. Clearly label facts, assumptions, and unverified hypotheses.
6. If a fix is authorized, create a regression test where feasible, implement the smallest change, and validate with lint/syntax/unit/ATC/LSP checks. Identify the target release and oldest supported ABAP release before authoring; on ABAP 7.40 or newer, actively consider modern ABAP syntax and verify each feature against that floor. Apply Clean ABAP naming where applicable, preserving SAP/project conventions. See the [Clean ABAP Cheat Sheet](https://github.com/SAP/styleguides/blob/main/clean-abap/cheat-sheet/CheatSheet.md) and [Names section](https://github.com/SAP/styleguides/blob/main/clean-abap/CleanABAP.md#names). Immediately before activation, `LintABAP` must succeed on the latest source for every ABAP code object in the exact activation request; re-lint after any source change and stop if lint is unavailable, fails, source is missing, or findings remain unresolved. For `ActivateMultiple`, activate only the exact reviewed and linted object set, never a broad inactive-object/package list. Check pending inactive objects with `GetInactiveObjects`, activate only when authorized, and never activate merely to run tests. Rerun the reproduction or strongest available runtime check.
